query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporating 5 vol% CaF2 nanoparticles into a CoCrFeNi high‐entropy alloy will form a stable, continuous CaF2 tribofilm during sliding that reduces interfacial shear and oxide formation, yielding at least 30% lower friction coefficient and 50% lower wear rate than the unmodified alloy across 25–800 °C under 5–20 N in dry air.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast, homogenized CoCrFeNi high‐entropy alloy without added solid‐lubricant phases
generation.intervention: Uniform dispersion of 5 vol% CaF2 nanoparticles in the CoCrFeNi matrix via mechanical alloying
generation.conditions: Dry sliding in ambient air (≈20% RH), temperatures 25–800 °C, normal load 5–20 N, sliding speed 10 cm/s
generation.structural_mediator: Continuous CaF2‐rich tribofilm at the sliding interface
generation.mechanism: The low‐shear‐strength CaF2 layer forms in situ and resists high‐temperature oxidation, maintaining a lubricious interface over the full temperature range
generation.predicted_outcome: Across all tested temperatures (25, 200, 400, 600, 800 °C), the CaF2‐doped alloy will exhibit ≥30% reduction in steady‐state coefficient of friction and ≥50% reduction in specific wear rate relative to the baseline CoCrFeNi
generation.baseline: Unmodified CoCrFeNi: μ≈0.6 at 25 °C rising to ≈0.8 at 800 °C; specific wear rate ≈1×10^–5 mm^3/Nm
generation.boundary: Temperatures 25–800 °C; normal load 5–20 N; ambient dry air (20% RH); sliding speed 10 cm/s
generation.uncertainty: Moderate uncertainty due to potential CaF2 grain coarsening/segregation at the highest temperatures and environmental variability

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare disks of CoCrFeNi with and without 5 vol% CaF2. Perform pin‐on‐disk sliding tests at 25, 200, 400, 600, and 800 °C under a 10 N load in dry air. Characterize friction traces, wear track volumes, and tribofilm chemistry.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the CaF2‐doped alloy fails to achieve both ≥30% lower friction coefficient and ≥50% lower specific wear rate than the unmodified alloy at three or more of the five test temperatures, the hypothesis is falsified.
